requirements.quote:
Aggregation reduces the amount of information that a BGP speaker must
   store and exchange with other BGP speakers.  Routes can be aggregated
   by applying the following procedure, separately, to path attributes
   of the same type and to the Network Layer Reachability Information.
requirements.condition: When using the described route aggregation procedure
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the procedure separately to path attributes of the same type and to Network Layer Reachability Information.
requirements.why_checkable: Aggregation inputs and per-type processing can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Routes that have different MULTI_EXIT_DISC attributes SHALL NOT be
   aggregated.
requirements.condition: Routes have different MULTI_EXIT_DISC attributes
requirements.why_checkable: Routes with unequal MED values expose whether aggregation is prohibited.

requirements.quote:
If the aggregated route has an AS_SET as the first element in its
   AS_PATH attribute, then the router that originates the route SHOULD
   NOT advertise the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute with this route.
requirements.condition: An aggregated route starts its AS_PATH with AS_SET
requirements.required_behavior: The originating router SHOULD NOT advertise MULTI_EXIT_DISC with the route.
requirements.why_checkable: The first path segment and presence of advertised MED are observable; the recommendation is preserved.

requirements.quote:
Path attributes that have different type codes cannot be aggregated
   together.  Path attributes of the same type code may be aggregated,
   according to the following rules:
requirements.condition: Path attributes have different type codes
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Aggregate attributes with different type codes together.
requirements.why_checkable: Attribute type grouping can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Path attributes that have different type codes cannot be aggregated
   together.  Path attributes of the same type code may be aggregated,
   according to the following rules:
requirements.condition: Path attributes have the same type code
requirements.required_behavior: May aggregate the attributes according to the stated per-attribute rules.
requirements.why_checkable: Same-type aggregation is a permitted operation subject to concrete attribute rules.

requirements.quote:
NEXT_HOP:
         When aggregating routes that have different NEXT_HOP
         attributes, the NEXT_HOP attribute of the aggregated route
         SHALL identify an interface on the BGP speaker that performs
         the aggregation.
requirements.condition: Aggregating routes with different NEXT_HOP attributes
requirements.required_behavior: The aggregate NEXT_HOP SHALL identify an interface on the aggregating BGP speaker.
requirements.why_checkable: The aggregate next hop can be compared to the speaker interfaces.

requirements.quote:
ORIGIN attribute:
         If at least one route among routes that are aggregated has
         ORIGIN with the value INCOMPLETE, then the aggregated route
         MUST have the ORIGIN attribute with the value INCOMPLETE.
         Otherwise, if at least one route among routes that are
         aggregated has ORIGIN with the value EGP, then the aggregated
         route MUST have the ORIGIN attribute with the value EGP.  In
         all other cases,, the value of the ORIGIN attribute of the
         aggregated route is IGP.
requirements.condition: At least one input route has ORIGIN INCOMPLETE
requirements.required_behavior: The aggregate MUST have ORIGIN INCOMPLETE.
requirements.why_checkable: Mixed-origin inputs allow the highest-precedence origin case to be checked.

requirements.quote:
ORIGIN attribute:
         If at least one route among routes that are aggregated has
         ORIGIN with the value INCOMPLETE, then the aggregated route
         MUST have the ORIGIN attribute with the value INCOMPLETE.
         Otherwise, if at least one route among routes that are
         aggregated has ORIGIN with the value EGP, then the aggregated
         route MUST have the ORIGIN attribute with the value EGP.  In
         all other cases,, the value of the ORIGIN attribute of the
         aggregated route is IGP.
requirements.condition: No input route has ORIGIN INCOMPLETE and at least one has ORIGIN EGP
requirements.required_behavior: The aggregate MUST have ORIGIN EGP.
requirements.why_checkable: Mixed EGP and IGP inputs check the conditional second-priority outcome.

requirements.quote:
ORIGIN attribute:
         If at least one route among routes that are aggregated has
         ORIGIN with the value INCOMPLETE, then the aggregated route
         MUST have the ORIGIN attribute with the value INCOMPLETE.
         Otherwise, if at least one route among routes that are
         aggregated has ORIGIN with the value EGP, then the aggregated
         route MUST have the ORIGIN attribute with the value EGP.  In
         all other cases,, the value of the ORIGIN attribute of the
         aggregated route is IGP.
requirements.condition: No input route has ORIGIN INCOMPLETE or EGP
requirements.required_behavior: The aggregate ORIGIN is IGP.
requirements.why_checkable: All-IGP inputs determine the fallback aggregate origin.

requirements.quote:
AS_PATH attribute:
         If routes to be aggregated have identical AS_PATH attributes,
         then the aggregated route has the same AS_PATH attribute as
         each individual route.
requirements.condition: All routes to aggregate have identical AS_PATH attributes
requirements.required_behavior: Retain that same AS_PATH in the aggregated route.
requirements.why_checkable: Input and aggregate AS_PATH values can be compared exactly.

requirements.quote:
- all tuples of type AS_SEQUENCE in the aggregated AS_PATH
             SHALL appear in all of the AS_PATHs in the initial set of
             routes to be aggregated.
requirements.condition: Aggregating routes whose AS_PATH attributes differ
requirements.required_behavior: Every aggregate AS_SEQUENCE tuple SHALL occur in every input AS_PATH.
requirements.why_checkable: Sequence tuples can be checked for membership in every source path.

requirements.quote:
- all tuples of type AS_SET in the aggregated AS_PATH SHALL
             appear in at least one of the AS_PATHs in the initial set
             (they may appear as either AS_SET or AS_SEQUENCE types).
requirements.condition: Aggregating routes whose AS_PATH attributes differ
requirements.required_behavior: Every aggregate AS_SET tuple SHALL have its AS value present in at least one input AS_PATH, as either AS_SET or AS_SEQUENCE.
requirements.why_checkable: Aggregate set members can be traced to source AS values independent of source segment type.

requirements.quote:
- for any tuple X of type AS_SEQUENCE in the aggregated
             AS_PATH, which precedes tuple Y in the aggregated AS_PATH,
             X precedes Y in each AS_PATH in the initial set, which
             contains Y, regardless of the type of Y.
requirements.condition: Aggregating routes whose AS_PATH attributes differ; an aggregate AS_SEQUENCE tuple X precedes tuple Y
requirements.required_behavior: X must precede Y in every input AS_PATH containing Y, regardless of Y type.
requirements.why_checkable: Relative positions of X and Y across paths can be compared.

requirements.quote:
- No tuple of type AS_SET with the same value SHALL appear
             more than once in the aggregated AS_PATH.
requirements.condition: Aggregating routes whose AS_PATH attributes differ
requirements.forbidden_behavior: An AS_SET tuple with the same AS value SHALL NOT occur more than once in the aggregate AS_PATH.
requirements.why_checkable: Duplicate aggregate AS_SET members are directly detectable.

requirements.quote:
- Multiple tuples of type AS_SEQUENCE with the same value may
             appear in the aggregated AS_PATH only when adjacent to
             another tuple of the same type and value.
requirements.condition: Aggregating routes whose AS_PATH attributes differ; an AS_SEQUENCE value occurs multiple times in the aggregate
requirements.required_behavior: Repeated AS_SEQUENCE tuples are permitted only when adjacent to another tuple of the same type and value.
requirements.why_checkable: The adjacency and type of repeated sequence values can be examined.

requirements.quote:
An implementation may choose any algorithm that conforms to
         these rules.  At a minimum, a conformant implementation SHALL
         be able to perform the following algorithm that meets all of
         the above conditions:
requirements.condition: Selecting an AS_PATH aggregation algorithm
requirements.required_behavior: May choose any algorithm conforming to all the stated AS_PATH aggregation rules.
requirements.why_checkable: Chosen algorithms can be checked against the listed output invariants without requiring a single exclusive algorithm.

requirements.quote:
An implementation may choose any algorithm that conforms to
         these rules.  At a minimum, a conformant implementation SHALL
         be able to perform the following algorithm that meets all of
         the above conditions:
requirements.condition: A conformant implementation supports AS_PATH aggregation
requirements.required_behavior: SHALL at minimum be able to perform the following described algorithm.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be inspected for support of the specified minimum algorithm.

requirements.quote:
- determine the longest leading sequence of tuples (as
             defined above) common to all the AS_PATH attributes of the
             routes to be aggregated.  Make this sequence the leading
             sequence of the aggregated AS_PATH attribute.
requirements.condition: When performing the minimum supported AS_PATH aggregation algorithm; first step
requirements.required_behavior: Determine the longest leading sequence of tuples common to all input AS_PATH attributes.
requirements.why_checkable: Common-prefix computation can be checked against paths with differing prefixes and segment types.

requirements.quote:
- determine the longest leading sequence of tuples (as
             defined above) common to all the AS_PATH attributes of the
             routes to be aggregated.  Make this sequence the leading
             sequence of the aggregated AS_PATH attribute.
requirements.condition: When performing the minimum supported AS_PATH aggregation algorithm; after determining the longest common leading sequence
requirements.required_behavior: Make that common sequence the leading sequence of the aggregate AS_PATH.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial aggregate prefix can be compared with the computed common prefix.

requirements.quote:
- set the type of the rest of the tuples from the AS_PATH
             attributes of the routes to be aggregated to AS_SET, and
             append them to the aggregated AS_PATH attribute.
requirements.condition: When performing the minimum supported AS_PATH aggregation algorithm; after preserving the common leading sequence
requirements.required_behavior: Set the type of all remaining input AS_PATH tuples to AS_SET.
requirements.why_checkable: The types assigned to source suffix tuples are observable.

requirements.quote:
- set the type of the rest of the tuples from the AS_PATH
             attributes of the routes to be aggregated to AS_SET, and
             append them to the aggregated AS_PATH attribute.
requirements.condition: When performing the minimum supported AS_PATH aggregation algorithm; after converting remaining input tuples to AS_SET
requirements.required_behavior: Append those converted tuples to the aggregate AS_PATH after its common leading sequence.
requirements.why_checkable: Aggregate tuple order can be checked at the suffix-appending stage.

requirements.quote:
- if the aggregated AS_PATH has more than one tuple with the
             same value (regardless of tuple's type), eliminate all but
             one such tuple by deleting tuples of the type AS_SET from
             the aggregated AS_PATH attribute.
requirements.condition: When performing the minimum supported AS_PATH aggregation algorithm; after appending remaining tuples, more than one aggregate tuple has the same value regardless of type
requirements.required_behavior: Eliminate duplicate values by deleting AS_SET tuples, retaining one such tuple as stated.
requirements.why_checkable: Duplicate elimination can be checked across set members and values shared with the sequence prefix.

requirements.quote:
- if the aggregated AS_PATH has more than one tuple with the
             same value (regardless of tuple's type), eliminate all but
             one such tuple by deleting tuples of the type AS_SET from
             the aggregated AS_PATH attribute.
requirements.condition: When performing the minimum supported AS_PATH aggregation algorithm; deleting duplicate values
requirements.required_behavior: Delete tuples of type AS_SET during this duplicate-elimination step.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Delete AS_SEQUENCE tuples as the means of eliminating these duplicates.
requirements.why_checkable: The specified deletion type can be checked in the duplicate-removal branch.

requirements.quote:
- for each pair of adjacent tuples in the aggregated AS_PATH,
             if both tuples have the same type, merge them together, as
             long as doing so will not cause a segment with a length
             greater than 255 to be generated.
requirements.condition: When performing the minimum supported AS_PATH aggregation algorithm; after duplicate elimination, adjacent tuples have the same type and merging does not create a segment longer than 255
requirements.required_behavior: Merge the adjacent tuples together.
requirements.why_checkable: Adjacent same-type segments and their resulting lengths expose the merge behavior.

requirements.quote:
- for each pair of adjacent tuples in the aggregated AS_PATH,
             if both tuples have the same type, merge them together, as
             long as doing so will not cause a segment with a length
             greater than 255 to be generated.
requirements.condition: When performing the minimum supported AS_PATH aggregation algorithm; considering a merge of adjacent same-type tuples that would generate a segment longer than 255
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary cases at 255 and 256 AS values check the merge limit.

requirements.quote:
ATOMIC_AGGREGATE:
         If at least one of the routes to be aggregated has
         ATOMIC_AGGREGATE path attribute, then the aggregated route
         SHALL have this attribute as well.
requirements.condition: At least one input route has the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute
requirements.required_behavior: The aggregated route SHALL also have ATOMIC_AGGREGATE.
requirements.why_checkable: Presence of the attribute can be compared between inputs and output.

requirements.quote:
AGGREGATOR:
         Any AGGREGATOR attributes from the routes to be aggregated MUST
         NOT be included in the aggregated route.  The BGP speaker
         performing the route aggregation MAY attach a new AGGREGATOR
         attribute (see Section 5.1.7).
requirements.condition: Aggregating routes with AGGREGATOR attributes
requirements.forbidden_behavior: MUST NOT include any input-route AGGREGATOR attributes in the aggregate.
requirements.why_checkable: Source AGGREGATOR attributes can be traced to ensure they are not copied.

requirements.quote:
AGGREGATOR:
         Any AGGREGATOR attributes from the routes to be aggregated MUST
         NOT be included in the aggregated route.  The BGP speaker
         performing the route aggregation MAY attach a new AGGREGATOR
         attribute (see Section 5.1.7).
requirements.condition: A BGP speaker performs route aggregation
requirements.required_behavior: MAY attach a new AGGREGATOR attribute to the aggregate.
requirements.why_checkable: Output permits a newly generated AGGREGATOR while preserving its optional nature.
